criteria.criterion: MCP tool failures carry the `error_envelope` discriminator — at minimum `error` and `message`, with `input` where a target was being resolved — delivered via `McpEnvelopeError` on the raised `ToolError.__cause__`
The error codes emitted over MCP are drawn from the SAME vocabulary the CLI emits, sourced from a single `error_code_for` classifier + `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES`; a code cannot exist on one interface only.
The failure shape is declared/documented alongside the success `outputSchema`s in `docs/output-schemas.md`, with a pointer added to `docs/mcp-reference.md`.
A test pins each emitted code, so rewording a human message cannot change the machine identity.
The three interfaces (library `error_code_for`, CLI envelope, MCP envelope) agree on the code for the same failure — verified by a cross-interface test, not by inspection.

Every MCP error — exception-raised OR returned (`_mcp_reads.py` explain_criterion, `_mcp_llm.py`) — carries an `error` code drawn from `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES`; the existing agent-branching fields (`kind`, `resolution_class`/`retryable`/`diagnostic`) are PRESERVED, not dropped.
Existing CLI envelope output is unchanged (no regression for current consumers), verified by a regression test.
Bug 'Give MCP failures the structured error identity the CLI already emits' is actually resolved: the reported defect no longer reproduces and expected behavior holds.
